outcome: PA-VTE location (lower extremities, cranial venous sinus, pelvic vein, pulmonary embolism)
cohort: The study included 122 women who experienced pregnancy-associated venous thromboembolism (PA-VTE) and delivered at Fujian Maternity and Child Health Hospital between January 2014 and August 2023, selected from a total of 171,898 pregnancies.
finding: The incidence of PA-VTE increased over the past decade, predominantly occurring postpartum, with main risk factors including advanced maternal age, thrombophilia, preterm birth, and elective cesarean section.
mod_finding: Elective cesarean section was identified as a main risk factor for PA-VTE, particularly during the puerperium period.
followup_time: Up to 28 days postpartum (for onset of VTE in puerperium)
gest_age: 5-39(+6) weeks (for VTE onset); 29(+1) to 40 weeks (for continued pregnancies, with preterm birth identified as a risk factor)
